title: Integration handoff digest - Week of 2026-07-19
content:
Meeting: Solutions Engineering + ProServices weekly coordination (aka Handoff Digest)
Date: 2026-07-19
Time: 10:30-11:15 PT
Attendees: Ava Martinez (owner), Samir Patel (SE), Lena Cho (ProServices PM), Diego Rivera (Field Eng), Priya Nair (SRE), plus three observers from customer success (names in Slack thread)

Purpose: quick sync on active customer integrations that are in handoff / early onramp. Focus on current blockers, short mitigation plans, and who owns next steps. This is intentionally terse so field teams can copy into customer-facing notes.

SUMMARY HIGHLIGHTS:
- Two customers (Veridian Health, Tidewater Analytics) are in canary validation this week; both on track for next-stage handoff but with different risk vectors (model latency vs network egress).
- One onboarding (BlueCove) has a critical tokenization mismatch that is blocking eval datasets — immediate remediation required from SE + Field Eng.
- We confirmed fallback routing for customers on Dedicated -> Hosted fallthroughs (policy updated in Routing Playbook).

CUSTOMER STATUS (ordered by near-term risk):

1) BlueCove (Priority: high)
- Stage: model evaluation / dataset ingestion
- Status: blocked
- Blocker: tokenization mismatch between customer's preprocessing and the model tokenizer (leading to 15–20% token-count variance; affects prefix caching and cost estimates).
- Impact: evaluation metrics unreliable; cannot complete `acceptance-eval` step. Potential delay to go/no-go by 5 business days if unresolved.
- Action items:
  - Samir to reproduce with customer's sample corpus and create repro container by EOD 2026-07-20 (owner: Samir).
  - Diego to coordinate a 1-hr pairing session with BlueCove ML lead Tuesday 2026-07-21 (owner: Diego).
  - Create a short-term pre-tokenization shim in the onramp pipeline if needed (owner: DevOps spike team; contact Priya).
- Notes: customer is amenable to adding a shim but prefers a permanent fix. Add to backlog: tokenizer mapping utility (low-effort library).

2) Veridian Health (Priority: medium-high)
- Stage: canary validation (private deployment variant)
- Status: progressing
- Blocker/Risk: PU latency spikes observed under longer sequence lengths (~4% of requests exceed 2x target p50). Trace points to KV cache misses and an unexpected sequence-length distribution during evening tests.
- Impact: could violate SLO for 1% of traffic during validation window; customer will pause rollout if not resolved by Friday 2026-07-23.
- Action items:
  - Priya to add temporary increased cache allocation and enable sequence-shape logging for one more day (owner: Priya; deadline 2026-07-20).
  - Samir to schedule microbench with same model variant locally and test with evening load profile (owner: Samir; deadline 2026-07-21).
  - If unresolved, propose a canary limit (max sequence len cutoff) and fallback to smaller model variant for long sequences (owner: Lina from ModelOps; ticket created: JIRA-OPS-4872).

3) Tidewater Analytics (Priority: medium)
- Stage: rollout planning for Dedicated capacity
- Status: on track
- Notes: committed capacity scheduled for 2026-08-02; need final approval on autoscaling burst policy and alert thresholds.
- Action items:
  - Lena to confirm SLA wording and autoscale policy with procurement (owner: Lena; deadline 2026-07-22).
  - SRE to add cost meters on token-level granularity for first 7 days of live traffic (owner: Priya; monitoring dashboard stub: in Observability team).

4) Indigo Retail (Priority: low)
- Stage: post-handoff monitoring (hosted API)
- Status: stable
- Notes: minor telemetry spike last week due to duplicated requests from a middleware bug in customer infra — customer fixed their side; no platform action required.

GENERAL BLOCKERS / THEMES NOTED THIS WEEK:
- Tokenization and preprocessing mismatches are becoming the most common early blocker across integrations (3/8 active deals). We should prioritize a small toolkit for SEs: tokenizer-diff tool + clear guidance doc.
- Network egress uncertainty with private deployments (customers asking for clearer bandwidth budgeting). Proposal: standard bandwidth-usage worksheet (see linked Confluence runbook).
- Canary observability: need clearer trace labeling for canary traffic so we can slice by model variant + rollout policy. SRE action item below.

DECISIONS / CHANGES MADE IN-MEETING:
- Routing Playbook: added an explicit step to configure fallback routing for Dedicated -> Hosted on capacity pressure. (Owner: Ava to merge to routing-playbook; PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing-playbook/pull/58)
- Onramp checklist: added mandatory tokenization sanity step prior to acceptance evals. (Owner: Samir to add checklist item; deadline 2026-07-21)

ACTION ITEMS (condensed):
- Samir: repro container for BlueCove + add tokenization checklist item (due 2026-07-20 / 2026-07-21).
- Diego: pairing session with BlueCove ML lead (2026-07-21).
- Priya: enable seq-shape logging + temporary cache increase for Veridian (2026-07-20); add token-level cost meters for Tidewater (2026-07-24).
- Lena: SLA and autoscale confirmation with procurement for Tidewater (2026-07-22).
- Ava: merge routing-playbook change and notify account execs (2026-07-20).
- ModelOps (Lina): be prepared with smaller model variant fallback for Veridian (ticket JIRA-OPS-4872).

OPEN QUESTIONS / RISKS (for execs and product):
- Do we want to fast-track a small tokenizer compatibility utility (yes/no)? Estimated 3 person-days. Product input needed for prioritization.
- Should we standardize a customer bandwidth worksheet for private deployments and include it in the handoff pack? Legal/procurement may need to sign off.
- Long-term: how do we classify tokenization divergences in our risk taxonomy (platform bug vs customer infra)? We need a consistent triage flow.

MEETING NOTES / LOGISTICS:
- Next meeting: 2026-07-26 10:30 PT (weekly cadence). If BlueCove blocker remains unresolved, schedule ad-hoc deep-dive Wednesday 2026-07-22.
- Notes posted to Confluence stub (see linked_artifacts) and Slack thread #onramp-handoff for daily updates.
- Use `onramp-scripts/repro` container as canonical repro for tokenization issues (see GH link).

APPENDIX (quick traces / snippets):
- Short trace: Veridian evening trace ID: trace-20260718-7732 — shows KV cache miss pattern on token index > 1024. Logged in observability.
- BlueCove sample: two sample documents attached in the repro container (sample_a.txt, sample_b.txt) — Samir to confirm canonicalization rules.

END OF DIGEST

Rough style notes: keep this doc minimal; copy relevant sections into customer-facing notes and add to account trackers. If you want me to reformat into a one-pager for customer execs, ping and I'll prepare a trimmed version.
